title: Heatline / Band-sparkline: legend reflow, density compression and screen-reader announce mode
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem statement: High-density time-series panels (multi-series telemetry dashboards) are producing heavy DOM/paint churns and noisy screen-reader output. Designers need a single compact visual — a hybrid 'heatline' / banded-sparkline — plus a lightweight legend and a controlled SR (screen-reader) 'announce mode' that summarizes deltas rather than repeating each point. Goals: reduce render cost for >50 series views, make legend behavior predictable across responsive breakpoints, and provide an accessible summary that doesn't overwhelm AT (assistive technology) users.

Design deliverables: visual spec for the heatline glyph and banding rules, responsive legend compression modes (inline, stacked, overflow popover), tooltip tokenization guidelines (short payloads for hover, expanded payload on focus), aria-live announce-mode copy templates, and a set of interaction states for keyboard and touch. Include tokens for spacing, micro-contrast, and minimum hit-targets.

Performance constraints: supports canvas-first rendering with offscreen buffering; fallback to SVG for small charts (<3 series). Must support incremental redraws for streaming data and a sampling policy to clamp per-frame series updates.

Success metrics: 40% reduction in median paint time for 50+ series views, legend reflow frequency reduced by 60% across responsive breakpoints, and positive accessibility usability test results with at least 4/5 participants preferring the announce summary vs raw point streaming.

References: UX research session notes, A11y audit 2026-02 (link in attachments), and a short engineering spike PR (ENG-8043) implementing a render-slice cache prototype.
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Desai: Initial brief posted after split-session with Observability PM. Attached early sketches in Figma for heatline and stacked-band variants.
2026-03-11 Jordan Cole: Wireframes refined — added three legend compression states (full, iconized, overflow). Requested token list from Design System for new micro-spacing and color steps.

2026-03-12 Maia Chen (A11y): Reviewed announce-mode copy. Suggested switching from continuous aria-live="polite" to a batched polite assert that emits only summary on series delta > threshold to avoid voice spam. Added checklist for keyboard focus summaries.

2026-03-12 ENG-8043 (Spike) comment: Render-slice cache prototype yields 35% paint reduction for 60-series synthetic workload on dev-n1. Needs integration with existing KV cache eviction logic. Plots show perf cliff at continuous reflow under layout width changes.

2026-03-13 Design review: Stakeholders (PM, Eng, A11y) agreed on: canvas-first heatline with band alpha layering, legend iconization with limited labels, and an explicit 'announce summary' keyboard shortcut (Shift+A) that triggers aria-live digest. Follow-ups: create content guidelines for announce-mode copy and finalize token names.

2026-03-13 Jordan Cole: Drafted token table (names and values) and added to attachments. Tokens include chart-gap-xx, legend-icon-size-xx, band-alpha-step-xx, a11y-announce-threshold. Waiting on Design System approval for naming conventions.

2026-03-14 Priya Desai: Pushed final visual spec to Figma and added a11y QA script for usability sessions. Marked ready for handoff. Requested eng review for hit-target confirmation and a small telemetry event to capture announce-mode usage.
2026-03-14 Maia Chen (A11y): Approved aria roles and recommended localization-ready summary templates. Note: avoid absolute timestamps in announces; use relative deltas.
